entries.note: 老 means old. In front of some people words it only shows respect.
姐 means older sister. In 小姐 it is a polite word for a young woman.

entries.teach: 太 means too, and in old titles great or senior. Doubled, it is a respectful word for a married woman.

entries.lit: someone who learns in the same place

entries.note: The characters were picked for their sound. On their own they mean platform and bay.
美 is short for the sound of "America". On its own it means beautiful.
英 is short for the sound of "England". On its own it means outstanding.
字 usually means a written character. In older Chinese it was also a second name an adult took, which is why it sits in this word.
Short for 印度尼西亞, which copies the sound of "Indonesia".
Both characters also mean happy, as in 歡喜.

entries.lit: no need to be so polite

entries.note: Also said 星期日.
明 means bright. With a day or a year it means the next one.
中 is short for 中國 here. 文 is used for both written and spoken language in language names.
英 is short for 英國 here. 文 is used for both written and spoken language in language names.
一 does not count a single item here. 一些 refers to an unspecified quantity.

entries.teach: 一 is one: things done 一起 are done as one. 起 does not add a clear meaning here, so learn the pair together.

entries.note: The name uses 鉛, but the core is graphite, not lead.

entries.teach: Learn this everyday noun as a unit with a light 西. With a full first tone on 西, dōngxī refers to the directions east and west.
Learn 便宜 as one word for a low price, the opposite of 貴. 便 is read pián here, not biàn as in 方便.
Learn 點心 as a food word, often used for something eaten between meals. The characters alone do not tell you what food it is.
entries.note: 點 can mean a small amount. It does not refer to clock time here.
點 is short for 點心 here.
常 alone already means often. Saying it twice is the everyday form.

entries.teach: Learn 還是 as the link between choices in a question. Use 或者 for alternatives in statements. Still and being do not explain this use.

entries.note: 氣 means air, and also the state of the air, as in 氣溫, temperature.
The Chinese name describes the reddish color of the brewed tea.
找 means returning the difference after payment here, rather than looking for something.
的 stands for people or things already understood. 有的 can introduce one group, followed by another 有的 for a different group.
包 names a bag or package here, rather than the action of wrapping.
裡 is a place ending here. It does not specifically mean inside.
樂 is pronounced yuè here. Its other reading, lè, means happy.

裡 is a place ending here. It does not specifically mean inside.
冰 supplies meaning. 淇淋 copies the sound of the foreign word cream.
可 alone can already mean but. 是 only fills the word out.
間 refers to a space or room here, rather than the gap between things.
太 means greatest here, not too. 陽 is the bright, sunny side of things.
空 is pronounced kòng when it means free time.

entries.lit: a machine for seeing by electricity

entries.note: 風 can refer to the appearance of a place, not just wind.
院 refers to a public building here, rather than a courtyard.

entries.teach: Learn 覺得 as a unit for personal impressions or opinions. 覺 is pronounced jué here, unlike jiào in 睡覺.

entries.note: 點 means a small amount here, not a time on the clock. 有點 usually introduces a quality the speaker finds undesirable.
息 can mean to rest or stop, as well as breath.
網 is short for 網路 here. The internet is a network, rather than a physical net.

entries.teach: Learn 可以 as a unit. Use it to ask permission or say that circumstances allow an action. 以 does not independently express permission.

entries.note: 後 places a day later in time here. The starting point is tomorrow.
前 places a day earlier in time here. The starting point is yesterday.
Said to someone as an order it means "do not". Said about yourself it means "do not want".
平 means ordinary here, rather than flat. 平常 can describe an ordinary thing or when something usually happens.
興 refers to enthusiasm or spirits here. 高 describes their level, rather than physical height.
It usually comes before a quality the speaker is not happy about.

entries.teach: 飯 points to meals and 店 to a business. In Taiwan, this word often names a large place where travelers stay overnight.

entries.note: 館 can name a building that provides lodging, not just a hall.
Short for 大眾捷運, mass rapid transit.

entries.lit: a vehicle once powered by fire

entries.note: 方 can mean an area or region, as well as a side.
封 is also the counting word for letters.

entries.teach: 方 and 便 have several senses. Learn this combination together, and use it for arrangements that suit someone or make a task simpler.
舒 suggests ease, but 服 does not mean clothes here. Learn the pair together for how your body feels or how pleasant something feels.

entries.note: 機 is short for 飛機 here.
開 can mean operating a vehicle or machine, as well as opening something.

entries.lit: the person who operates the machine

entries.note: 子 only rounds the word out here. It does not mean child.
去 means gone or past here, rather than to go.
明 means bright. With a day or a year it means the next one.
The sign on a product became the word for its brand.

entries.lit: to have a name people know

entries.teach: Learn this linking word together. It introduces a result, often after a reason introduced by 因為.
易 gives the useful clue here. Learn the pair together and use it before a task or an action that takes little effort.

entries.note: 公 marks metric units here. An ordinary 斤 in Taiwan is 600 grams, so the 公 matters.
間 can mean an interval in time as well as a space between things.
行 here means circulating or spreading, rather than going somewhere.
快 points to something happening soon. 要 marks what is going to happen, rather than what someone wants.
Say this to reassure someone after an apology or when a small problem does not matter.
It says I have let you down, so it is the word for sorry.

entries.teach: 對 can confirm that something is right. This phrase also introduces something you have just remembered and want to add to the conversation.

entries.note: 包 is a bag here, rather than the action of wrapping.
生 means student here. The word is also used casually for young people outside school.
生 means student here. The word is also used casually for young people outside school.

entries.lit: a collection of varied written pieces

entries.note: 的 helps 真 describe how true a statement is here. It does not show possession.
常 means usual or ordinary here, rather than often.
書 refers to writing here, rather than a book.
In a school setting, this refers to tasks a teacher assigns for students to complete.
對 means facing or opposite here, rather than correct.

entries.teach: 禮拜 first meant a weekly religious service, so it came to mean week. Add 一 to 六 for Monday to Saturday, and 天 or 日 for Sunday.

entries.note: 的 can stand for an unnamed thing here, or link 別 to a following noun.
Before a description, this signals a comparison. The other person or thing may be understood from the conversation.

entries.teach: 許 means perhaps here, as in 或許, and 也 adds little. Put the pair before a statement you are unsure of.

entries.lit: a test midway through the school term

entries.note: 日 is short for 日本 here. 文 can name a language, including its spoken form.
張 means to stretch here, rather than the counting word for flat things.
麼 is the same ending as in 這麼 and 什麼. At the start of a sentence, 那麼 means in that case.

entries.teach: 感 is to be affected by something and 冒 is to be exposed to it. Learn the pair together as catching a cold.

entries.note: 假 here is leave from work or school, pronounced jià. It is not jiǎ, meaning false.
燒 means burning. Here it refers to the heat of an unusually hot body.
生 here names a person with a learned occupation. It does not mean being born.
院 can name an institution as well as a courtyard.
生 can mean that something develops or arises, not just that someone is born.
意 here concerns the mind, rather than the meaning of a word.
朵 is an ending here. It is not counting flowers.
The whole word can also describe something wet, such as water. 乾 does not require literal dryness here.
得 here completes the verb. It is not the 得 that introduces how well someone does something.
要 alone can already mean if. 是 only fills the word out. 就 often follows in the next part of the sentence.
打 has several everyday verb uses. With 電話 it means making a call, not hitting anything.

entries.lit: carrying a burden in your heart

entries.teach: 忘 alone already means to forget. 記 means to remember and only fills the word out to two syllables. 忘記 and 忘 mean the same.

entries.note: 好 describes health here. 了 marks a change from the earlier condition.
嘴 alone already means mouth. 巴 only rounds the word out.

entries.teach: 已 supplies the time idea, but 經 is not a separate action here. Learn the pair together and place it before the verb.

entries.note: 卡 here copies the sound of English "card". It does not mean stuck.

entries.teach: 天 does not restrict the conversation to the sky or weather. Learn the pair together for casual conversation, without a specific topic.

entries.note: 差 here concerns a difference, not poor quality. The negative comes after 差 in this expression.

entries.lit: see each other face to face

entries.note: 以 links 前 to a time reference. Without a stated reference, the reference is now.
以 links 後 to a time reference. Without a stated reference, the reference is now.

entries.lit: what you have lived through and tested

entries.note: 樣 can mean a way of doing something as well as its appearance.
忙 here refers to work that needs doing, rather than describing someone as busy.
打 usually means to hit. In many words it is only a general doing word, as in 打掃.
是 completes this linking word. It does not assert that something is something else.
別 here means different. It is not the command word meaning do not.
點 can mean selecting particular items, not just marking a time on the clock.
相 here is an image or likeness, pronounced xiàng.
相 here means an image or likeness, pronounced xiàng.
去 gives the direction away from the speaker or the place being discussed.

entries.teach: These characters have senses beyond machine and ability. Learn the pair together, often after 有 or 沒有 when discussing whether an action is possible.
天 does not limit the talk to the sky or the weather. Learn it whole as casual talk about anything.

entries.note: 師 can name a trained professional, not only a teacher. 護理 combines protecting with caring for someone.
行 here names a business and is pronounced háng. It is not xíng, meaning to go or all right.
業 here means a course of study, rather than a line of work.

entries.teach: Public and managing do not specify the modern meaning. Learn the pair as a business noun, often following the name of a business.

entries.note: 老 is a respectful prefix here. It does not tell you the person is old.
班 can be a work shift as well as a school class.
班 here means a work shift. 下 marks leaving that shift.
麵 also means flour, and 包 can name a bun. A filling is not required in 麵包.
事 here refers to work or affairs, rather than a particular object.

entries.teach: 備 carries the idea of getting ready, but exactness is not required. Learn the pair together, followed by what someone is getting ready for.

entries.note: The old Chinese 時 was two hours long, so the shorter Western hour was called 小時. 點 gives a time on the clock.
With 鐘, 分 measures elapsed time. For a clock reading, 分 can follow the hour directly.
目 here means an item in a list, not an eye.
兒 here refers specifically to a male child. 子 is an ending, not a second child.
重 can describe importance as well as physical weight. 要 here means essential, not to want.
In Taiwan, the cold air also names the machine that produces it.

entries.lit: a hall for many kinds of things

entries.note: Used for visiting a place to look around it, such as a museum or a school.
口 can mean an opening, not only a mouth.

entries.teach: Learn this polite expression together. Use it before an interruption or request, or after a small mistake. It can also express embarrassment.

entries.note: 要 before an action can point to something about to happen, rather than something someone wants.
去 gives the direction away from the speaker or the place being discussed.
來 gives the direction toward the speaker or the place being discussed.

entries.teach: Learn this time expression together, rather than reading horse and on top literally. It goes before an action, including a future action, and does not mark past tense.

entries.lit: the record of what has passed

entries.note: The word also applies to invented events. They do not have to be true accounts of the past.

entries.lit: knowledge organised into branches of study
an intersection shaped like the character 十

entries.note: 口 can name an opening, including the entrance to a road.
上 places something within a setting here. It does not mean physically on top of the world.

entries.lit: crossing from one year into the next

entries.note: 會 means a gathering here, rather than being able to do something.
會 means a gathering here, rather than being able to do something.
樓 can mean a whole building as well as one floor of it.
多 asks about an amount here, as it does in 多少.
台 is short for 台灣.
The dough wraps around a filling.
麼 is an ending here. It does not ask a question as it does in 什麼.
教 means religion here, rather than the action of teaching.
意 means a thought or opinion here, rather than the meaning of a word.

entries.teach: 國 alone already means country. 家 means home or family. The two together are the everyday word for a country.

entries.lit: connections that let people pass through
entries.note: 交 can mean to connect or meet, as well as to exchange.

entries.lit: people who keep watch and inspect

entries.teach: A small heart is not the point here. Said on its own, 小心 warns someone to pay attention to danger.
生 points to birth, and 肖 means to resemble. Learn the pair together for the animal associated with your birth year.

entries.note: 打 helps form the action here. It does not mean hitting anything.
本 means a book here, rather than a root or a measure word.

entries.teach: Original and come do not form this expression literally. Use 原來 when you discover the real situation, often after expecting something different.

entries.note: 華 refers to Chinese ancestry or culture here, rather than citizenship.

entries.lit: to stand for someone and show their position

entries.note: 越 here is the old name of the Yue peoples of the south, not to cross over.

entries.lit: festival of the first full moon night
entries.note: 元 means first here, rather than money. 節 means festival, rather than a section.
會 means a gathering here, rather than being able to do something.
他 means other here, an older sense also found in 他人. It does not mean he.
放 means to release here, as in being released from work or school.
計 and 畫 can both mean to plan, rather than counting or drawing.
上 means previous in a sequence here, rather than up.
下 means next in a sequence here, rather than down.
學 means a school in these names for levels of education.
學 means a school in these names for levels of education.
學 means a school here. 大 points to a higher level of education, rather than the size of the buildings.
下 is a verb meaning to fall here, rather than a position below something.
下 is a verb meaning to fall here, rather than a position below something.
The characters copy an Indigenous name. They do not describe a pavilion.
The characters echo the Taiwanese pronunciation of the older name 洄瀾. Their separate meanings, flower and lotus, do not explain the name.

entries.teach: Root and come are the separate meanings. 本來 introduces an earlier situation or intention, often before you explain what changed.

entries.note: 後 means after in time here, rather than behind in space.
The characters were chosen for their Japanese sound, Takao, echoing the older place name. They do not describe height or strength.

entries.teach: A place name in Kaohsiung. 灣 means bay. Learn 西子 as part of the name, not as west and child.

entries.note: Short for 高速鐵路. 高 comes from 高速, high speed, and 鐵 from 鐵路, railway.
公 marks metric units here, rather than meaning public. A traditional 里 is a different unit.
公 marks metric units here, rather than meaning public. A traditional 尺 is a different unit.
公 marks metric units here. 分 refers to a division of length, rather than a minute of time.
上 means to attend here, as in 上課. 學 refers to school.

entries.note: 籠 means a steaming basket here. 包 names food wrapped in dough, as in 包子.
